If you pass in both `advertiser_id` and `advertiser_ids`, `advertiser_id` will be ignored. Valid when `report_type` is `BASIC` or `AUDIENCE`. A list of advertiser IDs. Max size: 5. Please be aware of the following information when working with this field: When `advertiser_ids` is used, we will return up to 20,000 IDs in response. The cutoff logic for IDs is based on the creation time of campaigns, ad groups, or ads in descending order, but we cannot guarantee that each advertiser will have an evenly distributed number of IDs.When `advertiser_ids` is used, the returned metrics data in the response will include `currency`, `timezone`, and `advertiser_id`. Different advertisers might have different time zones. You can use `multi_adv_report_in_utc_time` to determine whether the data returned should be set to the UTC+0 timezone for all advertisers or set to the local timezone for each respective advertiser. Different advertisers might have different currencies, and we will return the corresponding currency for each advertiser in the returned `metrics`. These metric data will be presented without a decimal point. For instance, a spend of "100 USD" will be displayed as 100 without any decimal indicator such as ".000".If you want to view the total added-up metrics for all advertiser IDs, enable `enable_total_metrics` in your request. The returned `total_metrics` in the response will include `currency`, `timezone`, and `advertiser_id`, but all with a value of `-`. Note:If you use `advertiser_ids` but do not include any ID dimensions in the dimensions field, we will return `0` as the value for `currency`, `timezone`, and `advertiser_id` and `-` as the value of cost-related metrics, such as `spend`, in the `metrics` object of the response.The advertisers specified in `advertiser_ids` should all belong to the same TikTok for Business user. Otherwise, an error will occur. Use [/oauth2/advertiser/get/](https://business-api.tiktok.com/portal/docs?id=1738455508553729) to retrieve a list of advertiser IDs that belong to the same TikTok for Business user. |

ID of a Business Center that you have access to. To get a list of Business Centers that you have access to, use [/bc/get/](https://business-api.tiktok.com/portal/docs?id=1737115687501826). |

| `cpv_video_duration` | `cpv_video_duration` | `"SIX_SECONDS" \| "TWO_SECONDS"` | No | No | The target video view duration. Enum values: `SIX_SECONDS`, `TWO_SECONDS`. |
| `feed_type` | `feed_type` | `"STANDARD_FEED" \| "TOP_FEED"` | No | No | Feed type option. Enum values: `STANDARD_FEED`, `TOP_FEED`. `STANDARD_FEED` refers to large inventory with normal CPM price while `TOP_FEED`refers to limited inventory with higher CPM price. |
| `rf_purchased_type` | `rf_purchased_type` | `"FIXED_SHOW" \| "FIXED_REACH" \| "FIXED_BUDGET"` | No | No | Buying type. Allowed values: `FIXED_SHOW`: Purchase to achieve a fixed amount of impressions.`FIXED_REACH`: Purchase to reach a fixed number of users.`FIXED_BUDGET`: Purchase with a fixed budget. |
| `budget` | `budget` | `number` | No | No | Budget. Required when `rf_purchased_type` = `FIXED_BUDGET`. Based on the budget amount that you specify, we will return the estimated values for other fields. |
| `purchased_impression` | `purchased_impression` | `number` | No | No | Impressions to be purchased, in the unit of 1,000. Required when `rf_purchased_type` = `FIXED_SHOW`. Based on the impression amount that you specify, we will return the estimated values for other fields. |
| `purchased_reach` | `purchased_reach` | `number` | No | No | Number of users reached to be purchased, in the unit of 1,000. Required when `rf_purchased_type` = `FIXED_REACH`. Based on the reach amount that you specify, we will return the estimated values for other fields. |
| `rf_campaign_type` | `rf_campaign_type` | `"STANDARD" \| "PULSE"` | No | No | When `objective_type` is specified as `RF_REACH`, use this field to set the campaign as a TikTok Pulse campaign, then you can get available premium contextual tags. Enum values: `STANDARD` (Reach & Frequency campaign), `PULSE` (TikTok Pulse campaign). If you set this field as `PULSE`, only one location ID (`location_id`) will be returned. Note: Do not pass in this field when `objective_type` is not specified as `RF_REACH`.You need to pass the `location_id` value returned in this endpoint to `location_ids` when you use [/adgroup/rf/create/](https://ads.tiktok.com/marketing_api/docs?id=1738235338194945) to create a TikTok Pulse ad group. |

| Field | Wire name | Type | Required | Nullable | Description |

| `location_ids` | `location_ids` | `Array<string>` | Yes | No | IDs of the targeted locations. targeting countries and/or regions. The location can be at the country or region level, the Province, DMA (Designated Market Area) or Metropolitan level, or the city level. Location targeting supports a single country / region only. If multiple location IDs are specified, they must from the same country / region. You can find the supported locations from [Reach & Frequency](https://ads.tiktok.com/marketing_api/docs?id=1738235311704065). For the list of location IDs, see [Location IDs](https://ads.tiktok.com/marketing_api/docs?id=1739311040498689). |
| `operating_systems` | `operating_systems` | `Array<string>` | No | No | Operating system. For enum values, see [Enumeration - Audience Operation System](https://ads.tiktok.com/marketing_api/docs?id=1737174886619138) |
| `network_types` | `network_types` | `Array<string>` | No | No | Network type. Default value: `unlimited`. For enum values, see [Enumeration - Audience Network Type](https://ads.tiktok.com/marketing_api/docs?id=1737174886619138). |
| `device_model_ids` | `device_model_ids` | `Array<string>` | No | No | IDs of the device models that you want to target. Currently only brand-level model IDs are supported. When this field is specified, `device_price_ranges` must not be specified. For enum values of device model IDs on different levels, please see [Device Models](https://ads.tiktok.com/marketing_api/docs?id=1737172880570369). Note: Only active devices (`is_active` = `True` in the response of [/tool/device_model/](https://ads.tiktok.com/marketing_api/docs?id=1737172880570369)) can be used to create ads. |
| `device_price_ranges` | `device_price_ranges` | `Array<number>` | No | No | Targeting device price range. 10000 means 1000+. The numbers must be in multiples of 50. Important: The upper limit you set will be added by 50 and the resulting new number will be used as the actual upper limit for device targeting. The actual upper limit is shown in the ad group settings in TikTok Ads Manager. If you set and get the price range of [0, 250], it actually means [0, 300]. |
| `carrier_ids` | `carrier_ids` | `Array<string>` | No | No | Carrier IDs. Use [/tool/carrier/](https://ads.tiktok.com/marketing_api/docs?id=1737168013095938) endpoint to get the enum values for this field. |
| `interest_category_ids` | `interest_category_ids` | `Array<string>` | No | No | Interest classification. If the interest is specified, users that do not meet interest target will be excluded during delivery. Do not specify if you wish to target everyone. Use [/tool/target_recommend_tags/](https://ads.tiktok.com/marketing_api/docs?id=1736275204260866) to get a list of recommended interest categories based on your targeting regions and your industries. Use [/tool/interest_category/](https://ads.tiktok.com/marketing_api/docs?id=1737174348712961) endpoint to get the complete list of interest categories. |
| `brand_safety_type` | `brand_safety_type` | `"NO_BRAND_SAFETY" \| "EXPANDED_INVENTORY" \| "STANDARD_INVENTORY" \| "LIMITED_INVENTORY" \| "THIRD_PARTY"` | No | No | Brand safety type for Reach and Frequency ads. Default value: `NO_BRAND_SAFETY`. Enum values: `NO_BRAND_SAFETY`: To not use any brand safety solution. Full inventory, which means your ads may appear next to some content featuring mature themes. `EXPANDED_INVENTORY`: Use TikTok's brand safety solution. Expanded inventory means that your ads will appear next to content where most inappropriate content has been removed, and that does not contain mature themes. In the next API version, `EXPANDED_INVENTORY` will replace `NO_BRAND_SAFETY` and will be the default brand safety option.`STANDARD_INVENTORY`: Use TikTok's brand safety solution. Standard inventory means that ads will appear next to content that is appropriate for most brands. `LIMITED_INVENTORY`: Use TikTok's brand safety solution. Limited inventory means that your ads will not appear next to content that contains mature themes.`THIRD_PARTY`: Use a third-party brand safety solution. To get the countries and regions that your ads can be deployed to based on your brand safety settings, use the [/tool/region/](https://ads.tiktok.com/marketing_api/docs?id=1737189539571713) endpoint. Note: Pre-bid third-party brand safety solutions are currently allowlist-only features. If you would like to access them, please contact your TikTok representative. |
| `contextual_tag_ids` | `contextual_tag_ids` | `Array<string>` | No | No | Contextual tag IDs. You can use [/tool/contextual_tag/get/](https://ads.tiktok.com/marketing_api/docs?id=1747747118654465) to get available contextual tags. Note: This is an allowlist-only feature. If you would like to access it, please contact your TikTok representative. Only supports `RF_REACH` as objectives (`objective_type`) at the campaign level. Not supported when `brand_safety_type` is set to `THIRD_PARTY`.Not supported when `feed_type` is set to `TOP_FEED`.If you set `rf_campaign_type` to `PULSE` in [/campaign/create/](https://ads.tiktok.com/marketing_api/docs?id=1739318962329602), then you must enter contextual tags of `PREMIUM` type in this field. |

## RfInventoryEstimateResponse

`object` model on the `json` wire format.

| Field | Wire name | Type | Required | Nullable | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `default_result` | `default_result` | `RfInventoryEstimateResponseDefaultResult` | No | No | Estimated inventory result. If you have specified a fixed value for `purchased_impression`, `budget`or `purchased_reach` in request, depending on the fixed value you have specified, we will return the corresponding predicted values in the `default_result` object in the response. For example, if you set `rf_purchased_type` to `FIXED_SHOW` and specify a fixed value in `purchased_impression`, then based on the impressions you set, we will calculate and return the estimated values for `budget`, `cpm`, `reach` and `average_frequency` in `default_result`. |
| `results` | `results` | `Array<RfInventoryEstimateResponseResults>` | No | No | Estimated inventory results for different budgets. In each result, the estimated impression, CPM, reach, frequency, daily cost, and frequency per person will be provided for the budget. The data structure for this object is the same as that of `default_result`. |

## RfInventoryEstimateResponseDefaultResult

`object` model on the `json` wire format.

| Field | Wire name | Type | Required | Nullable | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `base_info` | `base_info` | `RfInventoryEstimateResponseDefaultResultBaseInfo` | No | No | Basic information. |
| `daily_cost` | `daily_cost` | `RfInventoryEstimateResponseDefaultResultDailyCost` | No | No | Daily spend. |
| `frequency_per_person` | `frequency_per_person` | `RfInventoryEstimateResponseDefaultResultFrequencyPerPerson` | No | No | Distribution of impressions per person. Note: When the frequency cap determined by `frequency` and `frequency_schedule` in the request exceeds four times a day, the value for the `frequency_per_person` will remain unchanged. |

## RfInventoryEstimateResponseDefaultResultBaseInfo

`object` model on the `json` wire format.

| Field | Wire name | Type | Required | Nullable | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `budget` | `budget` | `number` | No | No | Total budget. |
| `cpm` | `cpm` | `number` | No | No | CPM (Cost per mille). Formula: `cpm` = `budget` / `impression`. |
| `impression` | `impression` | `number` | No | No | Total impressions, in the unit of 1,000. For example, the value of 110 for this field represents 110,000 impressions. |
| `reach` | `reach` | `number` | No | No | Number of users reached, in the unit of 1,000. For example, the value of 110 for this field represents 110,000 users reached. |
| `max_reach` | `max_reach` | `number` | No | No | Number of total bookable reach based on the specified feed type, targeting settings and campaign duration, in the unit of 1,000. For example, the value of 200 in this field represents an available inventory of 200,000 users. |
| `average_frequency` | `average_frequency` | `number` | No | No | Formula: impressions per person (`average_frequency`) = total impressions (`impression`)/ numbers of users reached (`reach`). |

## SearchAdNegativeKeywordAddParams

`object` model on the `json` wire format.

| Field | Wire name | Type | Required | Nullable | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `advertiser_id` | `advertiser_id` | `string` | Yes | No | Advertiser ID. |
| `object_type` | `object_type` | `"CAMPAIGN" \| "ADGROUP"` | Yes | No | Object type. Object type. Use this field to specify whether you want to create negative keywords for a campaign or ad group. Enum values: `CAMPAIGN`: campaign.`ADGROUP`: ad group. |
| `object_ids` | `object_ids` | `Array<string>` | Yes | No | Object IDs. Use this field to pass in campaign IDs or ad group IDs that you want to create negative keywords for. Max size: 50. Specify this field according to `object_type`: If `object_type` is `CAMPAIGN`, assign campaign IDs to this field. If `object_type` is `ADGROUP`, assign ad group IDs to this field. |
| `replace` | `replace` | `boolean` | No | No | Whether to replace all the existing negative keywords for the campaign or ad group with the keywords that you specify via `keywords`. Enum values: `true`: To replace all the existing negative keywords. `false`: To add new negative keywords. Default value: `false`. |
| `keywords` | `keywords` | `Array<SearchAdNegativeKeywordAddParamsKeywords>` | Yes | No | The list of negative keywords you want to create. Max size: 1,000. Note: For each ad group, you can configure a maximum of 10,000 negative keywords. |

## SearchAdNegativeKeywordAddParamsKeywords

`object` model on the `json` wire format.

| Field | Wire name | Type | Required | Nullable | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `name` | `string` | Yes | No | Name of the negative keyword you want to create. Length limit: 80 characters. The name needs to exclude the following special characters: [`!`, `@`, `%`, `^` , `(` , `)` , `=`, `&#123;`, `&#125;`, `;`, `~` , `&#96;` , `` , `?`, `\` , `&#124;`]. Otherwise, an error will occur. Note: Duplicate negative keyword names will be de-duplicated to only one unique name, and for each unique name you can only specify one match type. |
| `match_type` | `match_type` | `"PRECISE_WORD" \| "PHRASE_WORD" \| "BROAD_WORD"` | No | No | Match type for the negative keyword. Enum values: `PRECISE_WORD`: exact match.`PHRASE_WORD`: phrase match.`BROAD_WORD`: broad match.Default value: `BROAD_WORD`. |
